chunks: Yūnus, from Hishām ibn Ibrāhīm al-Mashriqī, from one who narrated it, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام used to flog for a small amount of nabīdh just as he flogged for a small amount of khamr, and he would execute on the third offense of nabīdh just as he would execute on the third offense of khamr.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amīr al-Muʾminīn, the title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.النَّبِيذِ: nabīdh, an intoxicating drink referred to in this legal context
key_terms.يَجْلِدُ: he administers flogging as a legal punishment
key_terms.يَقْتُلُ: he executes as the prescribed penalty in this context

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on drinking nabīdh compared to khamr in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام applied the same legal punishment to drinking a small amount of nabīdh as to drinking a small amount of khamr. It also indicates that repeated offense in drinking nabīdh incurred the same escalated penalty as repeated offense in drinking khamr, showing their equivalence in legal treatment here.
